To start a service using `systemctl`, you run the `systemctl start` command followed by the service name. If the service type is not specified, systemd looks for `.service` files by default.

For example, to start the `sshd` service, you would use:

```bash
[root@host ~]# systemctl start sshd
```

This command starts the service manually. Note that starting a service with `systemctl start` does not configure it to start automatically at boot time. 

To both start the service and enable it to start at boot, you can use the `--now` option with the `enable` command:

```bash
[root@host ~]# systemctl enable --now sshd.service
```
